title: Honeydew to join Workday
summary: Workday announced its intent to acquire Honeydew. Why AI that runs the core of the business needs a source of truth for meaning.
body_markdown:
A few hours ago I landed in Barcelona for Workday Rising EMEA, where today Workday[announced its intent to acquire Honeydew](https://newsroom.workday.com/2026-11-18-Workday-Announces-Intent-to-Acquire-Honeydew,-a-Semantic-Layer-for-AI-and-Business-Intelligence) .


But I’ll start with the call I made home after landing. It feels routine. You dial, and someone on the other side of the world picks up. The phone network is built for five nines: up 99.999% of the time. ChatGPT has only two nines.


Nothing about this call is probable. It hops across switches, undersea cables and cell towers, run by companies that compete with each other. Ship anchors cut cables. Switches crash. Storms knock out towers. Over just a few dozen years, we’ve built a system that can take unreliable conditions, and make it work, without fail.


When we started Honeydew four years ago, we made the bet that companies need a source of truth for meaning. No more dozens of definitions of ‘revenue’ spread everywhere. In hindsight that looks either naive (get everyone to agree on one definition?) - or prescient. Because once AI arrived on the scene, it needed a system of meaning to rely on. You can’t use it if it doesn’t understand the business.


We underestimated our task at the beginning. We were thinking of driving AI akin to Waze -[give it a map](https://honeydew.ai/blog/talk-to-your-data-loudly/) so it can only drive within it, and you don’t fall inadvertently in a lake. But completely trusted AI in business is much closer to the global phone network: it’s improbable, yet solvable.


The[Semantic Layer](https://honeydew.ai/blog/so-lets-talk-about-semantic-layers/) at the heart of Honeydew took one key aspect of improbable correctness and made it *deterministic* : we can help ensure that when AI says ‘revenue’, it is right. It gets the data right. You can trust it to make decisions based on that data. As we grew, we added more context layer abilities, more guardrails and many more product features, so AI works better overall. And by that, we made more areas of the business operable by AI.


Doing that for the most critical data means going where that data lives. That’s where Workday comes into the picture. Workday manages the core data of the enterprise: people and money. Data Cloud is where AI meets that data.


There are levels to how correct you need your AI to be. A so-so subject line costs you a few clicks. A wrong number in payroll costs someone their rent.


Workday is playing on hard mode. It’s a carrier network, not a walkie-talkie. Trusting AI to run the core of the business requires extraordinary solutions. Like Honeydew.


And it works in reverse. Once you have AI safely,[lawfully](https://www.workday.com/en-au/perspectives/ai/agent-cost-of-speed.html) , operating at this level, it is much easier to give it control over the everyday work around it. It will do it easily.


As we plan to join Workday (subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions), we believe that we built some of the critical pieces to get there.


This journey is made possible by our team, which is small and extraordinary, and made the hard things look easy. By our customers, who have pushed, and who constantly continue to push us to make the best semantic layer in the world. And by our investors, who have believed in us. Thank you all.


It took the phone network decades to get to five nines. AI will take less.


Team Honeydew
